Mark 3 helmet

Inside the Mark 3

A 3D-printed Iron Man helmet that opens by voice or button, answers questions using Claude, and lights up its eyes. Scroll to see the electronics inside.

Power

Battery and boost converter

One LiPo cell, stepped up to 5 V for everything else.

  • Battery1S LiPo, 3000 mAh, 3.7 V
  • Boost converterPololu U3V40F5 (3.7 V → 5 V)
  • ChargerTP4056 USB-C module
Brain

ESP32-S3 microcontroller

Runs the voice commands, servos and audio.

Motion

MG90S servos

Lift and lower the faceplate. Keep scrolling to open it.

Listening

INMP441 microphone

Sits inside the chin. Hears “open”, “close” and questions for Claude.

Sound

Amplifier and speaker

Plays Claude's replies and sound effects.

Lighting

Eye LEDs

Glow when the faceplate closes, go dark when it opens.

Wiring

Controller board

Connects every part on one circuit board.

Controller board · rev B

PCB design

The boost converter is the only 5 V source. The ESP32 sits behind a Schottky diode, so plugging in USB to program it never drives the servos.
